When they were written, in what order, and who proposed each date.
IN TIME
When they were written
All twenty-one on one line of years.
Each bar spans the widest range of dates the sources propose. No letter states its own date; 2 John and 3 John have no proposed date in these sources.
IN ORDER
Written order and Bible order
The order of the Bible beside the order of the earliest date proposed for each letter.
The Bible puts Paul's letters first, longest to shortest. By the earliest date proposed, James comes first (AD 40), then 1 Thessalonians and Galatians (AD 48). Click a letter.
PAUL'S YEARS
Paul's life and letters
Paul's life, and his letters where they were written.

The steps of Paul's life follow W. M. Ramsay's scheme of 1895 (the Chronological Index to St. Paul the Traveller); A. T. Robertson's 1915 encyclopedia scheme differs by a year or two at most points. The letters are drawn as ranges spanning the dates the sources propose. None of these years is stated in the Bible; Paul's own notes of time ("after three years", "fourteen years after") overlap and cannot simply be added together. Galatians 1:18 Galatians 2:1 2 Corinthians 12:2 Acts 20:31 [10][17]

Romans: when it was written

Written when Paul had finished preaching "from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum" and was about to carry the collection to Jerusalem, most likely in the three months in Greece of Acts 20. Moule dates it 58, noting that newer schemes move it to 56; Ramsay about January 57; Schaff spring 58; Easton early 58 (though elsewhere he says 55). Romans 15:19 Romans 15:25–26 Acts 20:2–3 [10][5][19]
